{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee of a covered employer under 29 CFR 825.110",
        "context_quotes": ["F000"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "An eligible employee must satisfy all three conditions: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service rules under § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005:F006"],
        "scope_text": "With respect to the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that, subject to paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted",
        "context_quotes": ["F001:F002"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section",
        "context_quotes": ["F005"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has had a break in service of more than seven years",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing).",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing purposes)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F008"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an absence from work is due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service",
        "context_quotes": ["F007"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), and for determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months",
        "context_quotes": ["F005:F006"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement",
        "context_quotes": ["F006:F009"],
        "modality_quote": "prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees",
        "context_quotes": ["F003"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "29 CFR part 785", "FLSA"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), where the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, not limited by methods of recordkeeping or compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all hours worked or in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA's principles",
        "context_quotes": ["F012"],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["FLSA"],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee returning from USERRA-covered service, in determining the employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave",
        "context_quotes": ["F003", "F012"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, such that a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has those hours added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (subject to special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541)",
        "context_quotes": ["F012"],
        "modality_quote": "has the burden",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "FLSA", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (such as full-time teachers of an elementary, secondary, or higher education establishment) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility for FMLA leave (subject to § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months",
        "context_quotes": ["F002", "F003"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement",
        "context_quotes": ["F015"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles",
        "context_quotes": ["F004"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a specific notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis",
        "context_quotes": ["F016"],
        "modality_quote": "not",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the worksite for that specific notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50 within 75 miles",
        "context_quotes": ["F016"],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer employs 60 employees in August but expects the number of employees to drop to 40 in December, and an otherwise eligible employee gives notice in August for leave beginning in December",
        "context_quotes": ["F016"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave in August for a period of leave to begin in December, even if the employer expects its employee count to drop from 60 in August to 40 in December."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee of a covered employer under 29 CFR 825.110
unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three conditions: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service rules under § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: With respect to the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that, subject to paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has had a break in service of more than seven years
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing).
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an absence from work is due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), and for determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), where the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, not limited by methods of recordkeeping or compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all hours worked or in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA's principles
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee returning from USERRA-covered service, in determining the employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, such that a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has those hours added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (subject to special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541)
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (such as full-time teachers of an elementary, secondary, or higher education establishment) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility for FMLA leave (subject to § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: When making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a specific notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis
unit_attributes.statement: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the worksite for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50 within 75 miles
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer employs 60 employees in August but expects the number of employees to drop to 40 in December, and an otherwise eligible employee gives notice in August for leave beginning in December
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave in August for a period of leave to begin in December, even if the employer expects its employee count to drop from 60 in August to 40 in December.
